skills.name: Writing a report on the treatment of patients; health slogans

note.text:
A report gives facts clearly and in order to someone who needs them.
Layout: a title; To: / From: / Date: / Subject:; an introduction (why you write and what you did); the findings in paragraphs (what you saw); recommendations (what should be done); your name.
Use the past tense for what happened and formal language.
A slogan is a short, catchy sentence that gives a message: “Clean hands save lives!” “A mosquito net a night keeps malaria out of sight!”

worked_example.problem: Plan a report to your principal about a visit to the district hospital.
steps: Introduction: the health club visited the hospital on {14} May to see how patients are treated.
Findings: patients are registered, then examined; the wards were clean but crowded; some patients waited many hours.
Recommendations: more benches and more nurses. Then a slogan to end.
worked_example.answer: Title → To/From/Date/Subject → introduction → findings → recommendations → name

cards.idea: A report starts with To, From, Date and Subject.
example: Subject: Visit to the district hospital

cards.idea: Give the findings in the past tense, in order.
example: The wards were clean but crowded.

cards.idea: A slogan is short and catchy.

questions.prompt: Put the parts of the report in order.

items.text: Report on our visit to the district hospital
To: The Principal  From: The Health Club  Date: 15 May
On 14 May, our club visited the hospital to see how patients are treated.
We found that the wards were clean but crowded.
We recommend more benches and more nurses.

paper_task.prompt: Write a report (about 150 words) in your exercise book to your principal about a visit to a hospital or health centre: how patients are received and treated. End with two health slogans.
model:
Report on our visit to Buea Regional Hospital
To: The Principal
From: The Health Club
Date: 15 May
Subject: How patients are treated

Introduction: On 14 May, twelve members of the Health Club visited the hospital with Mrs Ewane to see how patients are received and treated.

Findings: Patients first register at the reception and pay a small fee. A nurse takes their temperature and blood pressure, then they wait to see a doctor. The wards were clean and the nurses were kind, but many patients waited more than three hours on the corridor.

Recommendations: The hospital needs more benches, more nurses at the reception and a health talk for people who are waiting.

Slogans: “Clean hands save lives!” “Sleep under a net, keep malaria away!”

Tabe Ayuk, Secretary
checklist: My report has a title and To / From / Date / Subject.
My introduction says why we went and when.
My findings are in the past tense and in order.
I wrote two short, catchy slogans.
My sentences start with capitals and end with full stops.
